action.name: Queued: the place in line is the run's output

description: Fires on a review comment by an author in vars.trusted_authors (never the App itself). Same-repo, non-draft PRs of repos in vars.fixer_repos only; vars.fixer_excluded_repos overrides it. Adds the PR to the fixer queue (#35, d29: workflow queue-add); pr-fixer-dispatch starts its pr-fix run when it reaches the head of the line. Shares the per-PR concurrency key with the other pr-fixer-* rules (so a human push still resets the PR's attempt budget) but is not an attempt itself. The body must start with a command or mention the App in vars.fixer_comment_triggers (default /fix and @rules-culture-dev). Only while the PR is open. A trusted /fix (or mention) is a new request (d32): it resets the PR's attempt budget when it fires (resets_attempt_budget), and replaces a queued retry in place.
name: PR fixer: trusted review comment

on_failure.name: Hand back with the run link (once per chain)

params.body: PR fixer handed back ({{ run.error.code }}): {{ run.error.message }}

inputs.instruction: {{ trigger.data.author }} (a trusted author) left a review comment on PR {{ trigger.data.repository }}#{{ trigger.data.number }}. Work on the PR head branch {{ trigger.data.head_branch }} only. Fix the failing checks and the SonarCloud issues behind the failing quality gate, and address the review threads in the threads input (and no other thread). Never edit .github/workflows, never delete or skip tests and never add suppression markers. In threads_addressed, use each thread's thread_id exactly as the threads input gives it. For SonarCloud, follow sonar_note: when the quality gate fails, the sonar_issues input lists only the issues behind the failing conditions: fix exactly those; when the gate passes, it lists the issues on this PR's own new code: fix a listed new-code issue only if the trusted request names it. Never the rest of the Sonar backlog.
